summary: Correction round for v1.1 task 11.1 addressing the test-quality-reviewer findings TQ-11.1-1..6 and the security-reviewer findings SEC-11.1-1/SEC-11.1-3. Production behavior is unchanged; the changes are test depth, honest documentation of the actual secret-free guarantee, and one cosmetic unused-using removal. RC1 (TQ-11.1-1, HIGH): added FromLimitsBindsTheValidatedLimitsToTheCache, which builds ArrInventoryCache.FromLimits with distinctive non-default values (90 minutes, 7 records, 3 MiB) and asserts Ttl == TimeSpan.FromMinutes(90), MaxRecordsPerConnection == 7, MaxBytesPerConnection == 3 MiB, plus the default mapping; verified sensitive by temporarily swapping the record/byte fields and using TimeSpan.FromSeconds (test failed), then reverting. RC2 (TQ-11.1-2, MEDIUM): added ProviderFailureRetainedThroughTheCacheBoundaryNeverExtendsTheWindow, which stores through ArrInventoryCache.TryStore(..., lastError:) and asserts the failure-annotated entry is retrievable via TryGet, its ObservedAt/ExpiresAt/StaleUntil are identical to a non-failure store at the same observedAt/TTL (with the explicit boundaries ObservedAt, +10 min, +20 min), the records are preserved, and it is evicted at now >= StaleUntil; the existing entry-level test now also asserts records are preserved across WithFailure; verified sensitive by temporarily extending observedAt inside TryStore when lastError is non-null (test failed), then reverting. RC3 (TQ-11.1-3, MEDIUM) / SEC-11.1-3: renamed the name heuristic to InventoryCacheTypesHaveNoSecretNamedMembers and marked it secondary, and added InventoryCacheTypesExposeNoCredentialBearingMembers, a non-vacuous member-type denylist over ArrInventoryCache/ArrInventoryCacheEntry/ArrInventoryRecordObservation/ArrInventoryCacheState that unwraps generics/arrays and rejects ArrConnection, ArrConnectionConfiguration, SecretReference, SecretLease, PluginConfiguration, MetadataStateEntry, and MetadataStateStore; added LastErrorSatisfiesTheBoundedRedactedProviderErrorContract, which asserts ArrProviderError.Message is bounded to MaxMessageLength and that ArrProviderError exposes exactly Code/Retryability/Message. RC4 (TQ-11.1-4, LOW): added ByteBoundIsEnforcedAtTheActualEntrySize, a just-under/just-over pair at the real SizeBytes boundary (accepted at SizeBytes, rejected at SizeBytes - 1). RC5 (TQ-11.1-5, LOW): renamed OverBoundObservationSetIsNotCachedAndTheCallerKeepsDirectRead to OverBoundObservationSetIsRejectedWithoutDisplacingTheRetainedSet and added the observable contract that an over-bound store does not displace the previously retained set. RC6 (TQ-11.1-6, LOW): the distinctness test no longer relies on IsAssignableFrom between sealed classes; it scans the member types of ArrInventoryCacheEntry and ArrInventoryCache (non-vacuously) and asserts neither references MetadataStateEntry or MetadataStateStore, while keeping the per-item field-absence checks. RC7 (SEC-11.1-1, LOW): did not invent a new value-redaction policy; instead the documented contract now matches the actual guarantee in the ArrInventoryCache and ArrInventoryCacheEntry remarks and in docs/data-model.md section 6 and docs/architecture.md section 12: the entry's only free-text carrier is a bounded ArrProviderError, value-level redaction of that message is the producer contract (ArrProviderError is documented as bounded and redacted, ADR-020 clause 4), consistent with MetadataStateEntry.LastError, and the boundary does not claim to redact it. Also removed the unused 'using ArrTags.Matching;' from ArrInventoryCacheEntry.cs (reviewer 11.1-F2). The test class grew from 19 to 24 cases; the default suite is Failed 0, Passed 1387, Skipped 63, Total 1450.

known_limitations: The cache boundary is defined but not consumed. Exact behaviour: ArrInventoryCache is a standalone in-memory store with no DI registration and no caller; TryStore/TryGet are the only operations and no provider client or metadata reader uses them. Precondition: provider-client integration (11.2) and invalidation (11.3) are not implemented by this task. Consequence: reconciliation read volume and limitation F1 are unchanged until 11.2/11.3 land; docs/limitations.md F1 is deliberately left listed as unresolved.

No invalidation API is implemented. Exact behaviour: the boundary exposes only TryStore (replacement), TryGet, TTL expiry on access, and per-entry bound rejection; there is no Remove/Clear or webhook/post-scan/scheduled invalidation hook. Precondition: task 11.3 owns the ArrTags-side invalidation sources. Consequence: the TTL is the only freshness fallback in the model until 11.3 adds the event-based sources.

The byte bound is enforced against a deterministic conservative size estimate. Exact behaviour: ArrInventoryCacheEntry.SizeBytes sums UTF-16 string lengths of a subset of the canonical observation fields plus fixed per-record (256) and per-file (512) overheads, and TryStore rejects an entry whose estimate exceeds InventoryCacheMaxBytes; the record-count bound is the hard cap. Precondition: the estimate is used for accounting only. Consequence: InventoryCacheMaxBytes is a lower-bound accounting estimate, not an exact serialized/memory size; fields it omits (for example BadgeMetadata.MetadataFingerprint, ArrRecordIdentity strings, ArrProvider strings, audio features, and object overhead) can make actual retained bytes exceed the configured byte bound by a bounded per-record amount.

The inventory TTL is interpreted as the total bounded last-known-good lifetime with a fresh-first-half/stale-second-half split. Exact behaviour: ExpiresAt = ObservedAt + TTL/2 and StaleUntil = ObservedAt + TTL; the set is Fresh before ExpiresAt, Stale (usable, explicit last-known-good) until StaleUntil, and Expired at or after StaleUntil. Precondition: this mirrors the existing metadata last-known-good semantics that ADR-018 clause 5 says apply on provider failure and that docs/architecture.md section 12 already defines for metadata. Consequence: this interpretation is not silent; it is stated with rationale in docs/architecture.md section 12 and docs/data-model.md section 6, and the default 15-minute TTL and 10000-record / 32-MiB bounds are chosen, documented values rather than values fixed by ADR-018.

The entry's only free-text carrier, LastError, is stored as a bounded ArrProviderError without value-level redaction at the cache boundary. Exact behaviour: TryStore/ArrInventoryCacheEntry store the caller-supplied ArrProviderError unchanged (trimmed and truncated to 512 characters); value-level redaction of the message is the producer contract (ArrProviderError is documented as bounded and redacted, ADR-020 clause 4), consistent with MetadataStateEntry.LastError. Precondition: every producer supplies a bounded, non-secret message; all current producers are fixed code-owned strings and no caller exists yet. Consequence: a producer that violates its contract could retain a secret-bearing message; the cache does not prevent that. This is now documented in the ArrInventoryCache and ArrInventoryCacheEntry remarks, docs/data-model.md section 6, and docs/architecture.md section 12, and the RC3 test asserts the bounded/redacted structural contract rather than claiming value redaction; SEC-11.1-1 is thereby resolved by matching the documented contract to the actual guarantee (no new redaction policy was invented).

Host-guarded facts (JellyfinHostFact and package-content facts) remain skipped without ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR: 63 skips, identical to the pre-task baseline. Consequence: the live pinned-host confirmation is unaffected by this task and remains owned by the live-verification/release tasks.
